# One Workflow, Thirty Days: Proposal to Tamarack Instruments

**To:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel, Sponsor
**Engagement:** One Workflow, Thirty Days, AI Governance Academy
**Delivery instrument:** Consultant Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen/blob/main/consultant-workbook.md)

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client has a customer service chatbot deployed on its support portal. It is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line and plans AI sales forecasting for next year.

The Sponsor's stated objective is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

Three facts shape this proposal:

* **Audit finding.** An internal audit finding of June 2026 recorded that the Client has no inventory of AI systems.
* **Regulation.** The Client names the EU AI Act and GDPR as regulatory drivers.
* **Certification.** ISO/IEC 42001 work is to start next year, with the start date not fixed.

The Client has stated three constraints:

* Customer data must stay in the EU.
* The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff.
* A budget approval exists for this fiscal year.

A decision on this proposal is expected by 15 December 2026.

This engagement governs one workflow in depth. It does not by itself produce an inventory of AI systems. Whether its records help close the June 2026 finding is for the Client's internal audit function to judge.

## 2. The Workflow Proposed

**We propose AI visual inspection on the German production line** as the priority workflow, for three reasons:

* **It fits the Client's maturity.** The Client's AI maturity is Piloting, and this is the use case the Client describes as piloting. A thirty-day engagement can therefore examine a real operation rather than a plan.
* **It is the use case the objective names.** The Sponsor's objective refers to this workflow and its Q2 2027 production date. A Day 30 decision on evidence would arrive ahead of that date, provided the start date agreed after 15 December 2026 allows it. The start date is `Unknown`.
* **The other candidates fit less well now.** The deployed chatbot is a credible alternative candidate. Sales forecasting is planned rather than operating, so it offers no current work to baseline.

**The final selection is made in W02, not in this proposal.** W02 scores each candidate against the benefit scale's four factors:

* volume
* active human effort per unit
* rework and queue burden
* consequence of better or faster output

Two matters bear directly on this workflow:

* **Works council consultation.** Whether supervised AI cases in the inspection workflow touch production staff is `Unknown`. If they do, the Client's stated constraint requires works council consultation before Days 11 to 20. The timing of that consultation is `Unknown` and must be settled in W01. It may move the calendar.
* **EU data residency.** Whether the inspection workflow processes customer data is `Unknown`. The EU data residency constraint will be recorded in W01 either way.

## 3. The Thirty Days

The engagement runs thirty elapsed engagement days placed on Client working days, following the Workbook's thirty-day calendar. The Workbook plans that calendar for one workflow with five to six interviewees and 20 cases. That is the Workbook's planning default, not a headcount.

* **Days 1 to 5 (scope, W01 to W05 and W15 started).**
  * Charter W01 is signed by the Sponsor and the business owner of the workflow. Who holds the business owner role is `Unknown` and is fixed here.
  * W02 confirms the workflow selection.
  * Thresholds in W15 are started.
  * The works council consultation timing and the data residency constraint are recorded.
* **Days 6 to 10 (bounded rehearsal authorized, W06 to W11, W12 and W22).**
  * Rehearsal is authorized within bounds.
  * The operators, reviewers and technical owner of the inspection workflow are named. Each is `Unknown` until then.
* **Days 11 to 20 (matched baseline and supervised AI cases, W13 to W19, sponsor reports at Days 15 and 20).**
  * Current inspection work is measured against supervised AI cases on a matched basis.
  * Sponsor reports at Days 15 and 20 inform the Sponsor. They do not decide.
* **Days 21 to 25 (evidence challenged, W17 and W19 to W22 current).**
  * The evidence is challenged.
  * Failures and the actions taken on them are recorded.
* **Days 26 to 30 (independent challenge, sponsor decision and handover, W23 and W24 signed).**
  * The recommendation is independently challenged before the Sponsor decides. Who performs the independent challenge is `Unknown` and is agreed in W01.

**Stated audience.** The Client's stated audience is:

* General Counsel
* CISO
* Head of Quality
* Head of Data
* German plant manager
* two internal auditors

Which of them takes each Workbook role is `Unknown` and is set in W01. The Workbook roles are business owner, operator, reviewer, technical owner and receiving owner. Ravi Okafor and Ingrid Solberg attended the discovery call of 6 October 2026. Their roles are `Unknown`.

**Integration with incumbent management systems.** The Client holds an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and an ISO 9001 quality management system. The engagement's records are positioned as evidence within those systems, not as a parallel structure. The specific registers, processes or records they will attach to are `Unknown` until the Client identifies them. The engagement makes no certification or audit outcome promise, for ISO/IEC 42001 or otherwise.

**Supporting frameworks:**

* GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook)
* Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen)
* AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards), for board-layer reporting
* The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done), for acceptance

**Principles:** Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

**Regulatory orientation.** Regulatory content is orientation, not legal advice. Three items are flagged for external counsel:

* The classification of AI visual inspection under the EU AI Act.
* GDPR obligations arising from any personal data in the workflow.
* German works council co-determination requirements.

## 4. Deliverables

* **W01:** the signed charter.
* **W14:** the evidence register and decision pack.
* **W17:** the results record.
* **W23:** the Day 30 recommendation and decision.
* **W24:** the handover.

## 5. The Day 30 Decision

On Day 30 the Sponsor decides on evidence to **expand the specified scope, revise or stop**. The outcome of that decision is not promised. Final Liability rests with the Human.

* **Price:** by proposal.
* **Headcount:** by proposal.
* **Start date and on-site requirements:** `Unknown`. These include any presence at the German plant.

2. Name the business owner of the inspection workflow.
